title: Pre-render Change HTML to keep delivery within Workers Free CPU
context: Large Portable Text Change pages exceeded Workers Free request CPU even after bounded D1 queries. Request caching cannot make the first render or a private preview affordable. Content must remain in EmDash and interactive Blueprint components must remain available.
decision: Replace per-request Change body rendering with automated full SSG on EmDash save and publication lifecycle events. Use the official Portable Text renderer and existing typed-block components, preserving client islands. Stage both public and private HTML in a dedicated private R2 bucket, bound to renderer digest, content identity and exact revision. Requests verify current lifecycle metadata and signed preview scope before streaming an artifact; missing or mismatched artifacts fail closed without SSR or legacy fallback. Read PR status and statistics through a separate compact endpoint backed by the existing GitHub cache. This replaces the request-time rendering and build-free publication assumption of ADR-0124, while retaining that record's migration, archive and retirement requirements.

alternatives.option: Keep request-time SSR behind a cache
alternatives.reason: A cold render and private preview still exceed the Free CPU limit.

alternatives.option: Have an Agent manually render every update
alternatives.reason: Makes ordinary content editing depend on Agent availability.

alternatives.option: Patch SDK internals for incremental builds
alternatives.reason: Measured builds did not reuse prerendered pages; maintaining an upstream override costs more than the current full build.

consequences: Content updates require an automated build and artifact upload, but no Git content commit.
Publishing and preview may temporarily wait for a matching artifact; they never serve a different revision as a fallback.
Private artifacts require separate storage and must not enter public assets, media routes or CI caches.
Full local build success does not certify production Free CPU or account-wide resource quotas; activation remains separately authorized.
revisitTriggers: Build latency or frequency exceeds the Free budget.
The installed CMS supports stable incremental rendering without overrides.
Native CMS administration or metadata delivery exceeds Workers Free CPU.
